So, uh super excited just to continue to learn and play with these guys. >> Describe kind of the first uh times out here with the guys. >> No, it was it was cool. I mean, it was a new experience. Um you know, I feel like I could have had a better day, but you know, at the end of the day, it's practice. You know, practice ain't perfect. You know, as long as I'm getting better every day, you know, I think today as a whole was a good day. So, I'm I'm really happy. >> What do you say today? Uh just you know you know I've been out of football for a little minute. You know I've been training for the combine and training for to be a Olympic athlete rather than football player. So I say out of whack with that but as a you know football player it was kind of a little I guess I wouldn't say different but you know struggled a little bit but you know give it a little minute. I'll be back to show. >> Yeah. How different is it to get back into like learning teaching stuff like that? I mean I mean it's it's not like I was away from the game too long, but it's still still a little different. Of course, it's a little different from college, but you know, at the end of the day, it's football, so nothing nothing really changed for me. >> How good of a fit is this defense for you? >> I mean, I'm be honest, almost verbatim what I was doing in college. So, I mean, this defense is really fit for me. You know, I'm so glad that Vikings decided to take a chance on me to be a pinpoint in this defense cuz It's really who I am, you know. I'm a true nose guard. I'm a guy that's up to that's in the middle, you know, stopping everything. So, I'm I'm be honest. I fit really well to this defense. >> Most players play better loose, obviously. So, what do you tell yourself when you come in here? Like, you want to show your best. You want to jump right in, but you also want to be loose. >> Yeah. I mean, I don't know. You just got to be ready. Um, it's okay. It's okay to mess up. You know, you know, football is a game of imperfections. You know, you're not going to come in and be a Hall of Famer right away. to have that mindset. It's okay to mess up, but do it 100% at all times. So, that's the kind of message I say. >> What was the best thing you think you did today? >> Um, just going through the drills at at high speed. For me, that was that was my biggest emphasis. Give as much effort as I can. You know, even if I mess up, make sure I'm going 110 mph. So, that was that was my I think best thing I did today for sure. >> Caleb, first impressions. >> Yeah. No, it was amazing. Obviously, you know, this is a dream and so to actually be out here in your first NFL practice, it's really exciting. I >> mean, does it hit you that much more? I mean, clearly you did some celebrating draft weekend, but now that you put on the uniform, does it mean that much more? >> Yeah, definitely. You know, getting to wear the Vikings, you know, the logo, the name, all that means a lot more. >> How great of an opportunity is this for >> Oh, this is amazing. You know, it's a great staff here, great culture already here, a great city, great team. So, just being able to come in here with the vets in the room and just being able to soak up, you know, all the knowledge they have is really great. >> You say vets, but I [clears throat] mean, you played a snap in Northwestern. You played against a lot of NFL talent. I mean, just how ready are you for this opportunity? >> Yeah, you know, this is a completely different game than college. So, obviously, you know, in every aspect of my game, there's areas I can improve on. >> And just right tackle, left tackle. I mean, you have some position flexibility. >> Yeah, open to anything, you know, whatever Coach Carter wants to do, you know, I'm free to do whatever I want. So, >> are you sick of hearing about the the arm length? I mean, like in every walk of life, like we don't talk about arm length, but football, like everybody's talking about your short arms. >> Yeah. No, I mean, nothing I can do about it. I was born this way. You know, you can talk to my parents about it, I guess. But, you know, I'm comfortable with it. It's who I am. So, it's helped me get this far, so, you know, so why not? >> Yeah. I mean, it's I mean, that's the beauty is just watch the tape. I mean, you dominated Northwestern. Wasn't an issue when you were a >> Wildat. Yeah, definitely. So, I just, you know, just keep doing me. >> Perfect. >> I apologize for coming in late. Just one for you. Um, you know, how great is it sort of after getting through all of the pre-draft process and everything just to get back to football, get back out on the field? >> Yeah. No, it's amazing. Obviously, you know, there's a huge chunk where you're just like running in straight lines and doing this and doing that, but actually being able to do like football stuff and get with the team and get with your guys and do a bunch of drills, like it's very exciting. >> Awesome. >> When I'm on those visits, then it's like I'm by business, but now I can more or less relax and be myself and really get to work. So, it's been fun. I'm I'm enjoying every second of it. >> What do you know or think about Brian Flores already? >> I just know coach Coach Be is going to is going to get me and put me in the positions I need to do to help this team win. And I know the long history of, you know, him and Harry together. and I know, you know, the effect that they had with this defense. So, you know, I'm hoping I can step in and make an impact in in the way that they need me to. >> Did you guys run some of DFL stuff last year? >> Yes, absolutely. Uh, we ran a lot of that stuff at Miami. Um, you know, we watched it on tape and try to emulate it into our game. I think we did a pretty good job, but yeah, we definitely stole some stuff from him. >> Would you want to reach out to Harry? Have you heard from? >> Oh, yeah. We we've had a little bit of contact uh, you know, recently. We talked a little bit. um you know ready to meet him in person again and and just connect with him and they soak up as soak up as much as I can from him. >> I know when the coaching staff says they want you guys to be prepared above the neck as well, but it's a fine balance when you come out here and you want to show what you can do. How do you handle that? >> Um >> I just be me. I just come out here and enjoy the game. Like you know, you know, Coach Flo said it earlier this morning. You know, we've been doing this our entire life. So don't take the fun part out of it because you put a new logo on. So, I'm just enjoying every process of it and and I don't know how to stop smiling here. So, >> how much did you admire and what did you admire specifically about Harry? >> Um, you know, being from Tennessee, you know, we didn't have a lot of guys that came up in the area that I lived in. Um, so, you know, to have a beacon of light or somebody that we could look to and be like, "Hey, you know, this guy's doing it. Um, why can't I?" Um, but, you know, watching his career unfold as I've grown up, you know, we hear about him all the time at home. even though he's a couple times over, we still hear about him. So, you know, now that I'm in the position that he was in, you know, I just want to take maximum advantage of the of the situation that I'm in and hopefully be a beacon of light for the kids back home. >> Oh, it was a privilege. You know, my new teammates, everything about them was amazing. We all came out here with the same energy and the same focus and the same goal. You know, tomorrow is not promised for none of us. So, what can we do today to make our impact that impactful to where we see each other face again? And so just being out here and seeing all the guys fly around and move in a purpose that they moved with, man, that that's that's what it's like, man. That's that's what it's about being in this league today. >> Anything stand out about getting to be out there working with Brian Flores, Coach Alexander, and just the coaching staff in general? >> Just how efficiently everything goes, you know, especially transition from college to the NFL. Being out here, everything, you know, they know what they wanted. They know what they wanted to see. And so the execution wasn't nothing less than that. you know there's a standard and it's either you raise you don't just meet the standard you raise it and you know being out here for the one day I noticed that you know and how efficiently everything move and how you wanted to look like one unit >> you had mentioned that you did some pre-draft work with Jacobe Thomas what's it been like reconnecting with him a little bit >> it's always good seeing a familiar face you know I I train with him during the pre-draft process and so being out here and now he's the safety I talk to and we communicate you know it almost felt like we played at the same college together. So, you know, it's always good to have a familiar face out there and, you know, it just kind of makes everything move more swiftly. Have >> you met any of the veteran quarterbacks yet and got to meet the guys on on the team already? >> Uh, I haven't met any of the vets yet. I I definitely have. I'm looking forward to meeting all of them though, you know, and just being a sponge around those guys. I know I don't know it all yet. And, you know, these guys, they have the experience. They've been through it. They've been through the adversity. So, it's a lot I can pick up from them. So, I'm just ready to meet those guys, be a sponge, and take everything I can and apply it to my next step. >> For you, like what's the the biggest area you want to grow in before your first proseason starts? >> I would have to say being being a leader on a team full of vets, you know, cuz some rookies, as a rookie, we come in, you know, we don't know it all, and that can kind of lead us to being shy or not being as vocal. But I'm going to be that same guy who, you know, not only raises a standard but exceeds it, you know, and not being scared to have a voice and stepping up and being that guy like this rookie is dependable on the field and off the field, too. So, he's not just he may be a rookie, but he acts like a vet and his approach to the field and life is like a vet. you know, our coach, the running back coach here, coach Mockkins, uh, talks about those guys and those and those things they do throughout the day, uh, you know, to get their bodies and and theirelves up to par. And so, uh, just being able to, you know, hear coach talk about those guys and see how those guys operate and move is definitely cool. Uh, you know, starting Monday, we'll all be mixed together and in the mix with each other. And so, uh, definitely can't wait for that opportunity. I'm super jacked and ready to go for that. >> What's coach Bob been like so far? >> Great. Uh, just real honest with me. uh you know having a coach that's very honest uh you know makes this a little easier uh because I know exactly what I have to do and so uh he's been straightforward with me um just letting me know that it's certain things I got to get better at um and continue to improve on and so really just uh you know having a coach like that um you know with positive words and you know good things to say um and not you know just being real is just definitely something that you know I appreciate from coach >> what type of things like what what are going to be the points of emphasis for you as you prepare to play in this league? Yeah, I mean he just make sure my alignment's right. Just small things, alignment, uh make sure I hear the call, hear everything that's being uh presented in the huddle. And so, uh just being on tune of that, watching film, uh doing recovery, getting my body right, you know, and so uh just being uh uh somebody that I can trust and somebody that I can lean on, uh to help me during this process is definitely uh how Coach Makers has been helping me along this process. >> Mind, how great of an opportunity is >> Awesome, man. Uh you know, I come from the middle of nowhere. Uh single mom. She has five boys including me. And so, uh, you know, be I'm the first out of my high school, county, everything to do this, uh, go to college, do all of that. And so, uh, just being able to, you know, be a ear, you know, be the voice for my community back home, for my for my brothers, for my family, uh, has just been amazing to me. And so, just being able to step into this light, um, and and my family members see me playing at the biggest stage that it could be, um, is definitely an opportunity that, you know, I'm super grateful to have and ready to attack, uh, every day. You've talked a couple times about your mom and just kind of the sacrifices that you saw her make. I mean, how exciting, rewarding, whatever the word is. Um, is it to kind of share this with her, you know, be able to to share this experience with her to kind of, you know, have her watching after all she's done for you? >> Yeah. No, definitely a great great experience, great opportunity. Uh, you know, my mom is 100%. She has my back. Uh, but she also knows that, you know, I got to lock in and focus. And so, you know, before I left, I kind of told her like, "Hey, don't call that don't call that phone a little bit. Like, let me get let [laughter] me get adjusted. Let me get settled in." Because I was a little homesick yesterday and all. So, um, and she was like, "Okay, baby. I got you." And so, she'll send me a text every now and then and just let me know that she's still supporting me, watching me, and, uh, you know, looking over me. And so, for that, I appreciate them. And, uh, like I said, I'm super excited to, you know, represent that Clayborn name, but also just represent the Minnesota Vikings. Well, the fact that you've always been a leader and you've made it this far, what do you think you bring to the table in terms of balancing that but yet like diving in full force? >> Yeah. You know, I think, you know, from the playing my playing ability, you know, I bring a lot of explosiveness to this to this offense. Uh the ability to uh break long runs, make people miss in tight spaces, uh to generate those explosive plays, uh to take the ball to the house, you know, 60 70 yards. And so I think uh from the physical standpoint um that's what I bring to the Minnesota Vikings from that standpoint. But like just overall emotional, mental, uh I think, you know, I'm a great teammate. You know, I love my teammates. I want to know about the guys uh and what they have going on. And so uh really an energy guy in the locker room. Uh like to crack jokes and laugh and stuff. And so, you know, really just uh you know, being the best version of myself for the guys around me is, you know, what I'm most excited about. And like I said, I can't wait to get to work >> with your field. Okay, I was starting guess with your field vision and and kind of ability to sense and hit those holes. Is that is that something that just sort of comes naturally like is that something that you developed? >> Yeah, you know, I would say uh freshman year of uh college, I definitely struggled a little bit along the once I started to understand the game um of football. It definitely allowed me to uh limit the thinking and uh you know just play fast and full. And so uh you know over time I definitely developed the skill but uh you know I ultimately got to this point uh you know by doing those explosive things and uh it become a natural one. So uh it's a mix of both. [laughter] >> There's one more one more. Um just uh kind of going back to your mom like what do you remember sort of about being young and the way that she was involved in your football journey? >> Yeah you know I would say so my mom worked three jobs. uh to this day she still works three jobs and so you know I vividly remember you know when I would walk to go work out my mom would be leaving to go to work you know and so uh it's she wasn't as much hand on my football career but uh just seeing how she attacked her business is uh what allowed me to continue to attack mines and so uh she was motivating doing her own thing and you know for that I'm appreciative >> how special is this >> yeah it's unbelievable opportunity you know there's a lot of family history here so it's definitely really cool to be stepping foot out here myself. >> What was it like when you told your dad, "Hey, the Vikings are inviting me. I'm gonna be a Vikings turkey camp." >> He was he was very excited. You know, he's ultimately just proud of me for anything. I I can't I can't ask for a better role model. So, it was definitely a really cool moment. >> I mean, even aside from that, though, like this is a great opportunity. How great an opportunity is this for you? >> Yeah, it's unbelievable. Um, you know, I I feel very confident in my abilities and I feel like I got to showcase that today. Um, unbelievable coaching staff here, just staff in general everywhere. Um, I can't I can't say enough good things about this organization. I'm beyond blessed that I had an opportunity to come here. >> You're just a sponge or you want to ask a lot of questions. We got KOC counting all these great coaches around here. >> Yes. I mean, it's it's it's surreal. You know, you see all them on TV, you understand the greatness that they all, you know, have within themselves, but to be able to be here and absorb all that information from them, it's it's second to none. >> What's the journey been like? I mean, from Buffalo High School in Iowa State and South Dakota, like it's been a long time, right, that you were in high school. >> Yeah. No, it's definitely, you know, I've hopped around. I've hopped around the place, but I've learned a lot. learned a lot about myself and learned a lot about, you know, what what what my path is, what it's what it's going to be, what it needs to be, stuff like that. So, um, you know, I wouldn't change it for the world. >> And I know obviously your journey has to be your own, but just what have you kind of been able to take from your dad's experience and how has he been able to help you kind of prep for this? >> Yeah. Yeah. I think he's he's instilled a lot in me mainly, you know, in the quarterback position, like the leadership, um, that those intangibles that you can't really teach. Um, I've gotten that from him from day one, just confidence and, you know, the love for competition. So that's kind of in the Bowman blood, I'd say.

title: Kevin O'Connell on Vikings Rookie Minicamp, Adding Jauan Jennings, Caleb Banks Update, O-Line Group
text: Uh hey guys, appreciate you coming out to uh our rookie mini camp. Um want to first start out today and uh just uh make sure I pay personally pay my respects to Joe Sensor and our organization is doing the the same thing as well. Um you know obviously we care greatly about you know the the players that have played for this organization that have helped forge the path of this organization to where we are today. and uh just wanted to start out and uh just mention his his family and and keeping him in our thoughts and our prayers. Uh but also very thankful for the five seasons that that Joe was a part of this organization and the many years after that. Um you know, being involved in in multiple capacities with the organization. You know, obviously on a lighter note, uh excited for uh I want to wish the best to the Wolves tonight and the Wild tomorrow and and then the Wolves again on Sunday. uh always a a very uh fun time of year in the Twin Cities when uh both those organizations are are fighting it out in the playoffs and and setting a great standard uh for for us as well. And so I want to wish them the best of luck. You guys know my philosophy on, you know, this camp is is really designed to uh do a lot of things at once. We want to give opportunity to to guys that had not been signed uh on a try out basis. We want to, you know, we always have uh some veterans that are that are willing to join us for the for this time. Um and then we have our college free agents we signed and then ultimately this is the first uh you know the first chance we get to get on the grass with many of our draft picks and at least get them going in the offseason program. did one day this year just because uh you know you guys know I'm a big data guy and the data was telling me over the years the stress we were putting on these guys going Friday, Saturday and then uh they tend to run a little uh run a little hot on Monday when they're out there with the veterans for the first time and we've just had some kind of little things bump pop up over the years from a soft tissue perspective. So wanted to get a little bit longer of a practice today. I thought the guys handled it really well. We got some good work in. Uh now they'll, you know, they'll start preparing to join the big group uh on uh on Monday. Uh just a update on Caleb. Caleb Banks is doing great. Um you know, got some more positive information here as as he reported to uh to Egan uh in the last couple days and and very much looking forward to him uh you know, really establishing a real great plan with our medical staff and the coaching staff. uh you know obviously on the medical side getting healthy and on the coaching staff side. How can we uh you know push uh Caleb from an above the neck standpoint to be that much more comfortable when he does get healthy, but he gets a great chance this uh this spring and summer to get strong uh and build himself up for uh you know the uh the multiple aspects we think he can help our team uh in the fall. And then uh you know ultimately wanted to touch on you know coming to terms with Jawan Jennings last night. really excited about that. Um, hosted him on a visit. Had a great visit with Jawan and uh, really enjoyed my time I got to spend with him and he's a player that I've always, you know, from afar had a lot of respect for. U, you know, he's obviously brings size to the room. Uh, brings a level of play style and physicality. the guy loves playing football and and uh and and also you know the catch radius and the competes and the production uh that he's had to so to be able to sign a player um you know after a pretty patient approach uh you know allowing ourselves to have some opportunity in the draft if it came to us but always with a real mindset on Jawan being a target and just want to highlight Rob and the staff that the job that they did uh getting that one done and and uh we'll be excited expecting him uh hopefully to arrive on Sunday to get going on Monday which will be which will be uh big for us. So, um appreciate once again you guys coming out and I'll turn it over to you guys. >> Then just when it comes to Jennings, like how important was that for you with his the size that he brings, just something a little bit different than what you had in that room? >> Yeah, you guys, you know, over the four years, you've seen how especially with Justin and with Jordan, you know, we we need some we we need a a unique aspect to that room. uh not only for you know that quote unquote number three position, but we've talked a lot throughout the the process over the years of you can't just be one thing, you know, because we move Justin around. We move Jordan around. Uh you got to be able to be a slot receiver. You got to be able to do some of those jobs on the early downs that we ask of that player. Uh you got to be able to line up on third down when you're you're one of the few players that might be single covered in manto man. You got to be able to win. You got to be able to make contested catches and uh you got to be able to do something with it after the catch. catch and Jawan does all those things. I think Vikings fans are going to fall in love with watching this guy play football. Just passion and and the physicality that he plays with and um you know, you can tell I'm excited about it and and can't wait to get him here. >> Caleb, when you talk about kind of stressing him above the neck, just like how much can he gain from just being out here even if he's not participating? I think, you know, the the positive is you you normally worry early on, even with like uh you know, Jake Gold for for instance, we've got some thoughts in how his the ultimate picture may look, but you want to allow him because he's doing it physically uh from today on, you want to allow him to get comfortable in a spot before maybe you start throwing multiple things at him. Uh with Caleb, he doesn't necessarily have to worry about the physical side of it right now other than just getting healthy. Uh, so we can, you know, hopefully challenge him to, you know, learn multiple spots that that coincides with his versatility to align in in different impactful spots along the D line. So, um, you know, he can take part in walkthroughs. He can take part in, you know, the rookies are on a little bit different schedule. It's funny how that works out uh than the veterans in the offseason program, so we get them for more time. Uh, so I'm I'm really encouraged by uh just, you know, not only Caleb's enthusiasm to get going, um, but obviously the coaching staff and their plans for him as well. >> Does the good news about him uh change the timetable, Kevin, for him to get back on the practice field? >> I don't how does that work? >> I don't know if it changes the timetable. I just think we're happy with where he's at, you know, all things all things considered. and and uh you know it might and I can keep you guys updated on that as we go, but you know, you're really already into uh you know uh a chilly month of May here. Um so uh you're already into a point where we want to have our eyes on that end of July date so he can hopefully have a seamless transition into training camp and work backwards from there. Um is kind of the hope and you guys know how I handle a lot of the team aspect of the spring from a standpoint of really teaching learning phase. Um it, you know, hopefully we can it could coincide with him maybe getting a little bit of work there, but uh don't want to get ahead of myself at all. >> With Jennings, to what degree does his history as a run blocker kind of make him attractive? You mentioned he has a unique aspect to that. >> Yeah, I mean there are some unbelievable clips over the years of of not a of if I said doing his job, that would be a wild understatement. Um there's an emphasis that he wants to go out and play with a certain kind of play style uh that I think uh you know we've seen uh at times with different guys over the years and we've kind of pieced the room together in different ways to maximize each guy's skill set. But that's what's so exciting about Jawan is he truly is a combo receiver that can line up on the ball as a single. He can line up and you know in in formations with other receivers, stacks, bunches. He understands uh you know I got a lot of respect for the offense that they run in San Francisco. He understands how it all works together from marrying the run and the pass and the jobs you do in the run game directly you know equaling some targets in in different phases of of the marriage of the run and the pass. So um yeah I'm I think it's a matter of uh you know a veteran player that uh has clearly put on tape over the years that he can have uh great impact in in multiple roles and it gives us depth. It gives us the ability to overcome, you know, any potential injuries that may pop up along the way. And it also sets a great standard for uh the room with having Justin Jefferson, Jordan Addison, Jawan Jennings, and then a bunch of really young players that we're really excited about and want to let those guys grow and develop and compete. >> What about Ryan Nielsen? Do you think it's going to be good for these young guys in that? >> Yeah, I've already felt it, Alec. uh just, you know, even throughout the weeks of uh or the week of the first week of phase two, he's such a teacher, you know, and and really if you if you're around him long enough and you get to watch him work, you just see a guy that is teaching the smallest of details to equal great gains. Uh you know, helping guys play with more power, helping guys that uh need to play a certain kind of way. you know, maybe they're a player that is good, you know, on the move and and kind of creating edges via our scheme, but we're going to need him to also play to a higher standard as a rooted kind of gap defender. Uh, he knows how to do that. He knows how to kind of get the best out of players and and do it in a way where he's pushing these guys, but uh, in a way where you see these guys respond to it. It's been awesome to see. And Keith Carter's been the same way with the O line. You know, I our O line had a phenomenal first week. Uh it was great to see those guys uh you know getting after it and working. I mean uh that's the one thing about both those guys is they cherish their time on the grass uh with their players and they're going to maximize it. >> Was saying that um he grew up idolizing Harry obviously and that he's looking forward to meeting him in person and picking his brain. So a do we know anything about Harry coming back and b um how important would that be for someone like Harry to give his knowledge? It's good for Jacobe to be breaking news here on his first day. No, we uh we don't know anything. Uh the the communication's been ongoing. Um and don't really have an update on that, but I do think, you know, that came up on Jacob's visit here, his 30 visit, and just talking to him about that, pulling up some tape of Harry, especially towards the tail end of last year, some of the things he was doing uh quarterbacking the defense, and it got Jacobe really excited. It also allowed us to see uh another layer to to him from a mental side of playing the game. Uh that uh projects really well in our defense. >> What were you hoping to get out of the two quarterbacks you invited, especially Cooper? >> Yeah, I love, you know, a lot of a lot of times, you know, as a you're you're putting together these these camps and you you would love to make sure you can use this as a productive time. We got four quarterbacks we really like on our roster. Uh, but as I told Cooper, this is a this is a great it's almost, you know, it's it's it's almost like a a free agent visit. You know, he gets to know us, we get to know him. He's played a lot of football over the years in in the National Football League and and had a very productive times in in his journey. Um, and we get him for, you know, our time here. And, uh, I told him there's nothing that ever can come out of this from a negative standpoint getting to step on the grass and and put on a Vikings helmet. We now know Cooper. he knows a very very small portion of of some of the things we do offensively, but um I think it can open up that world to him of uh if there's an opportunity in the future um you know he can make that a really positive situation for himself and become our first phone call. So I thought uh I thought it was a real positive thing and then for Aiden um you know what a what a cool story uh to have him here. I thought he threw the ball well too uh once I got past the lefty spin of the football. Um but uh but yeah, I thought both those guys, you know, all things, you know, were throwing a lot at them. Sometimes it doesn't necessarily always look like football, but having two productive guys at that position driving the driving the show certainly made it a productive day for the group. >> What's Cooper's reaction that initially when you said, "Hey, I want you to come to a rookie mini camp." >> Yeah, I I mean, you're you're uh in many ways, you know, you're hoping you don't get the phone hung up on you. Uh but the way you you know I think he looked at it as a great chance to get some work and um you know it's a it's a chance to call plays in the huddle, break the huddle and go through progressions and and be like my my respect level for guys that are willing to be uh do the uncomfortable things for for the sake of their not only their own personal growth and development but uh making a positive impact on us and and on me and and that's what he did. the GM search obviously ongoing. Uh he's not going to let you slack off. title: Caleb Lomu Introductory Press Conference at Gillette Stadium | 2026 NFL Draft First Round Pick
text: Well, we'd like to welcome everyone here today. It's an exciting day for me personally and our family. Uh it's it's really the official kickoff of our new season. I can't wait for us to start playing again. We're so excited with our number one draft pick. Uh I think you'll all like chatting with them. Um, you know, he he told us a nice story that he flew on a plane that his uncle was the pilot. So, how great karma is that >> coming here today? So, you got >> flying here today. Excuse me. Thank you. I was and I I'm just thinking of the great energy he has and uh I think uh we're going to have a lot of fun this year. Anyhow, it's my great thrill to introduce Caleb Lamu. Raise your hand. How's it going? >> Good. How are you? >> Doing great. >> Caleb Chris Price with the Boston Globe. Can you just share what the acclamation process has been like since you first got the call on draft night? >> I mean, yeah. As soon as I got that call, you know, the whole surreal feeling of draft night and all that. um didn't really sink in until that next morning when I woke up and really processed it that whole night was kind of a blur. Um, but you know, got the all the excitement, emotions of that night, then laid in bed that night, woke up the next morning. Then it really settled in that I was a Patriot and it all, you know, hit me all at once. And so leading up to that moment till now, you know, it's all been, you know, excitement, just ready to, you know, get here, finally be here, uh, meet everyone, meet all the great people, coaches, uh, players. And so it's been all positive. It's been all, you know, super amazing of draft night until until this moment. Caleb, down here in the front, what is your uncle's name, pilot? >> Yeah, it was my uncle Curtis. And so he it was a funny story. He texted my mom about the day, so two days ago, and he was like, "Hey, what flight is Caleb on? You know, I just got assigned to this last minute flight to Boston." So, ended up being the exact same flight. And so I got on the flight and he's the type of uncle to where he's going to embarrass you a little bit. So I knew he was coming so my family told me, you know, film it. And so I got on the plane. I was kind of just waiting. And then of course he got on the intercom, started talking. And then he actually brought I thought he was going to go just talk about me, but he brought me up to the front and gave me like this flight pin of my first flight with him. Um, just telling everyone who I was and proud uncles what what he was saying. So it was awesome. >> Two quick follow-up questions on that. Could you spell his name for us just so we have it correct? >> It was C U R T I S. >> Okay. Curtis. And last, did I get it right, Curtis? >> Yeah. And Taylor. T A Y L. >> And what airline? >> American Airlines. >> Coming from Arizona. >> Coming from Arizona's redeye flight last night. Um, all the way here. >> Sorry, not Taylor. Tanner. I don't know why. T A N E R. Tanner. Caleb, how you doing over here on your left? >> Don't you love the detail for Mike Reese getting all that stuff down? See, I love it. >> That's just a high level. >> Getting all the little details in >> high level of professionalism up here. Every day is just like this, too. >> Oh, yeah. That's what I've heard. >> Um, I wanted to ask you about a little bit of football. >> Your comfort level moving over to the right side. >> Yeah. And will that be at all disorienting? And do you still view yourself at some point as saying, you know, I could play left tackle, you know? >> Yeah, for sure. I mean, I just feel myself as a tackle just in general, left or right side. Uh just happened to play left in college. And that's kind of just what I got, you know, comfortable to just playing those, uh, three years at left tackle at Utah. Um, my first year there, I was kind of a swing tackle. And so um you know I feel comfortable out left but also been working at right these past couple months. So feel just as good um on the right side as well. So either tackle position I'm happy to play and feel comfortable playing. >> And have you had a chance to to speak with Will Campbell yet and devel develop any kind of relationship or with any of the offensive linemen? >> I have. So him and a few other guys texted me uh right after I got drafted. send me just a, you know, welcoming text and then also been able to do some meetings with um the O line kind of just getting install and all that ready and so got to talk with them just over Zoom though. Um haven't met any of them yet in person so excited for that opportunity but was able to text with a few of them and then just talk over Zoom. >> Caleb down here, uh Sophie with Patriots Wire, I'm just curious, is there anything behind obviously the video of you dancing in the draft went pretty viral. Um, was there anything any inspiration behind that draft uh that dance or anything like that? >> Yeah, so that was uh that was an interesting moment. That was just at the combine, you know, all the media stuff that they were doing there. They put me up on the stage along with a lot of other people. They had all the cameras just like this and they go, "All right, for 10 seconds, just do whatever and we're going to film you." And so I was saying like like what what should I do? And they were like, "Just do whatever you want." And I didn't just do it once. They made me do that like four different times. It made me walk from the back of the stage up to the front doing the exact same thing. Um, you know, that moment I hated it. Hated that moment, but I was like, "Okay, I'm up here. I'm just going to do whatever my body does." And so that's where there's no really backstory to that. That was really just what I was feeling in the moment. And so, of course, they decided to use that as as a dance that they posted. So >> yeah, it was not my best work, but it was it was something. >> Caleb, over to your right, Taylor Kyle for CLNS Media First. Congratulations. Welcome to New England. >> Appreciate it. >> Um, watching your tape, man, you look like an absolute natural in pass protection. I know you've got a cousin who's in the league, so I'm curious. Where exactly does that come from, that ability, and was it helpful having a little bit of those NFL roots? >> For sure. Um, that's kind of how I've always just played. You know, my game's just been always try to be fluent out there and calm, collected. That's just how I feel I play best when I'm just, you know, I'm calm, my mind's working. Um, I'm be able to think faster, react quicker to everything. And so that that's just how I play my game. Um, that's preparation leading up the week before and also just, you know, pregame. Um, getting my mind right, just knowing when I go out there and I'm calm, I know what I know and I'm prepared to go out there, I know everything else will come with it. as long as I just play confident, play free, I know that's when I play my best ball. And so, um, that's always just how I've played from, you know, when I started playing football. And that's how I'll keep playing, um, coming into the NFL. >> Hi, Caleb. Two-part question. Uh, how would you describe your interactions with coach Vrabel since you've been drafted? And what can you tell us about the map on draft night? >> Yeah, with coach Varel, it's been amazing. You know, the energy that a guy brings to, you know, this team, you can kind of just feel it. I haven't been here yet, but I can already feel it and you can see it just out on the field. The energy that he brings, that's what you want in a head coach and it's what you want for a team and that's why, you know, I believe they went so far last year. Um, so everything's been awesome with him. The map, that's a funny story. Um, so my wife just made a just printed out a little map of, you know, the US um, and then the teams of each state. And so we just hung that up, put on the wall, and then everyone in the family could just get a little sticky note, put their guesses of where they thought I was going to go. And it was a funny story. My wife actually chose New England. She was the only one who put um her name up on the Patriots. And so that was a sign right there of where I was going to go. But yeah, that's the story behind that. Everyone could just go up and pick where they thought. Um I'm LDS and faith. And so usually when you get your mission call, you you do the same thing. So you you have the whole map though and you kind of choose where you think that person's going to go. And so it's kind of the same thought process behind that. Um but it was just the the NFL team. So it's pretty cool. >> Hey Caleb, welcome to Foxboro. >> Thank you. >> Uh just what has day one looked like for you since you hit the ground? Have you been able to take all this in? And then how anxious are you to just get under a Patriots helmet and get to practice tomorrow? >> Yeah, it's been amazing. Had a red eye just like we were talking about. Got in early this morning. I was able to go to the hotel and get some sleep. I'm not really able to sleep on plane. So, I was able to get some good rest this morning. Um, but then came here, you know, met with Nancy. Guy, I'm sure you guys all know Nancy, lovely lady. Um, was able to meet with her, then just meet everyone else uh that was in the building. Kind of just getting a tour, went to EQ, did all that fun stuff. Did some um, you know, paperwork and all that. And then this is definitely the coolest part right here, you know, coming to the stadium, being able to actually be in here and see everything, you know, have my picture up there and name. It's it's pretty cool to see and so it's been it's been an awesome day. Got uh to meet with both the crafts, Robert and Jonathan Craft. So that was an amazing experience uh meeting with them. And so you know this whole day has been amazing. This weather can't complain with the weather. I mean it's perfect. And so uh just a first positive day, you know, it's awesome, but definitely ready to get under that helmet and and get ready to play some ball. >> Hey Caleb, Alex Bar, 985. Uh you mentioned talking with the offensive line a little bit. What it's been like with Mike Frabel, Drake May, have you what kind of interaction have you had with him and what have your initial impressions been of him? >> Yeah, so he actually texted me as well after draft night. That was that was awesome to see, you know, young quarterback, which you know, I love the energy that he brings to the team, the talent that he has. You know, I excited to be able to protect for him and play with him. you know, he's such a young guy with so much, you know, left of him and experience and talent and so I'm excited to be able to play for that for many years. You know, he's young and so he'll be here for a long time. You know, I plan on staying here for a long time as well and so very excited to get that. Excited to be able to meet him here soon um in person, but so far it's been positive. >> Hey, Caleb Mark Daniels from Mass Lab. As you embark in your first off season and first season in the NFL, what are your goals for the short term and and then the long term here? Yeah, for sure. You know, short term coming in as a rookie, you know, I'm gonna be a sponge, learn everything that I can. Um, talk with the vets, see what they, you know, their routine that they have. Being here for so long, you know, NFL is a lot different from college with, you know, mental and physical, it's a way longer season. And so, um, having that routine is very important. So, cling on to a a vet and getting as much advice and, you know, information that I can get. Coming in, you know, I know nothing. And so I'm coming in learning as much as I can um on the field, off the field as well. And so that's that's my main goal short term just to come in learning as much as I can and and long term of course to get back to where we were last year and and get a win. Um Super Bowl is my biggest goal that I want for me and the team. Um that's a what I've always wanted since I was a kid and this is the type of team that's that has done it. know we can do it and and will do it and so I've you know very confident in this team to get back to where they were and very excited to be part of that. >> All right, Doug Kai from Boston Herald right here. Uh first of all, you've never been to New England before, right? >> I have not. >> Uh what are your initial impressions of New England? >> I mean it's been awesome. I haven't seen too much. You know, when I landed this morning, it was a little bit glooier and so a little bit dark. Didn't really see much. Just had to drive over here. Um, and then just once it started, uh, really just seeing like around here, around the stadium and in this place. So, I'm excited to be able to actually go explore whenever I can and see more of New England and explore and so haven't seen much, but so far it's been it's been awesome. >> Uh, second question, I know Tom asked you about playing right tackle. Elliot Wolf mentioned that you could play across the line. How would you feel about playing or cross trainining at guard a little bit? >> Yeah, any position that they need me at, you know, I'm willing to play and would love to play. uh they play the you know there's five guys there's five positions and any position that you know I can contribute to to help the team I'm going to do that and so and just to get on the field and get some playing time you know that's that's the goal and uh whatever position that they need me to play to be able to get on the field and play I'm willing to do >> Caleb after the draft you talked about coach Whittingham and and some other people have had impacts on your life is there someone outside of that another coach or a mentor who you looked up to who you might want to acknowledge at this point to say, look, you know, I'm not here by myself. This is someone who got me here. >> Yeah, of course. You know, my family's the biggest thing. All those coaches over at Utah, Coach Wood and Coach Harding, importantly, that's why I went to Utah because of those guys. Um, you know, they were great coaches. My family, you know, that's the most important one. My wife that I have now. Um, and it's my family all they're with me through the whole ride, you know, since I started playing football when I was young. Um, and until now. And so, they they've been the biggest help. Um, and I'm big in my faith. Of course, I know I wouldn't be here uh without God above and I'm so grateful for that. I know I'm in this position because of him. Um and I I never take that for granted. And so I know that he's the biggest help and that's why I'm here today. And so there's so many I could go on and name so many people, but you know, those are those are the main people and uh that, you know, I want to acknowledge and do that. >> Two final questions. >> Yep. To the right again. >> Thank you. Uh this is a team that's not shy about its use of extra offensive linemen, their jumbo packages. Have you ever played any type of skill position in your past? Have you ever toted the rock, caught a pass, anything like that? >> Yeah, back in my glory days with flag football when I was younger. I was a receiver and and a quarterback. And so sometimes I still think I'm that even though I'm, you know, 300 and something pounds. I'm a lot bigger, but I I still think back on those days when I can throw the ball pretty good. You know, I'm I'll get out and show that on the field whenever I can if I get a ball. But, you know, I'm a big man, but I still think I can move pretty well. So any opportunity I get to do something else, um my job's to block and I'll do that every single time. But if they give me an opportunity to do something else, you know, I'm always ready for that. But I did play other positions. Yeah. Just in flag football, uh tackle football, you know, it's been offensive line, defensive line, some tight end a little bit, but they always threw me on the line because I was a little bit bigger. And so tackle football has always been, you know, offensive lineman. >> Last question. Sophie Roll. >> Hi Caleb. I'm just curious. So you mentioned the map. You mentioned your wife picked the Patriots. Um, what was her reaction when you were drafted? >> Yeah. So, it's funny. She was actually the first one to see. So, my phone, you know, was on my lap and I got the call and she was the first one to look over and actually see it. Maybe she processed it. She I was just talking about the draft cuz they the whole process was kind of kind of weird cuz they traded up and I we had no idea. And so when I got the call there was another team up and we're like, is it is like is it them? But she actually saw it said MA and then she kind of worked some things out in her head. But she was the first one to see it and just like I was talking about the map, she she picked that and so she always talked about the Patriots being one of her top spots that she wanted to go and you know maybe she she guessed it spot on and so she was you know very excited. You can see it in her reaction when when we got the call and you know she's was very excited. She's excited to get out here and kind of experience everything as well. >> One more. Does it come with gloating rice? And also, what's it like to just be able to share this entire experience with her? >> Oh, that's that's the biggest thing. You know, we're we're newly wed. We've been married two months today. So, it's kind of sucked at first. It's been a lot of long distance for just getting married. And so, that part's hard, but you know, that's what comes with the job and the experience. And she's been more than more than helpful of this whole experience. And she's, you know, everything that, you know, I need. She's she's always there and everything that, you know, comes with football. She knows it's a lot of time away. And so, you know, she's she's in for the ride and it's it just helps so much. You know, it' be awesome to get her out here um once she's able to. And then it's she's helped me a lot get to this point. Um so, all thanks to her and um all the effort and love that she's put into, you know, my career leading up to this moment. >> Thank you guys.

title: Brock Rechsteiner on tryout, wrestling lineage | Saints Rookie Minicamp
text: Rock, obviously, you're a guy who's comes in, you know, Jacksonville State, trying to work your way in as a receiver. How things going for you the first couple of days? Um I've I've been I think I've done good with today. I think I've shown what I can do on the field. I've just been locked in. You know, when you're in a situation like this, you know, what are you looking to to I guess gain from it? Because obviously you want to catch the coaches' eyes. What are you looking to work on? Um just really just playing with a chip on my shoulder, playing hard, playing fast, showing them what all I can do, and then just learning, going against NFL level competition, what I can get better on myself. You know, are you looking at yourself as an underdog in this situation? Because, you know, you're undrafted and, you know, you got to work your way up the ranks. >> Yep, you know, for sure. I feel like I've always been underdog. Um I was a special teams PWO, preferred walk-on, coming out of high school, earned a scholarship, got the starting job, and then now I'm here pretty much doing the same thing. Yep. Now, obviously, you've got the famous lineage. >> [laughter] >> And I'm sure everybody's been working on you about that. You know, how does that help you, I guess, you know, having a a famous dad who's an athlete, you know, a guy who who, you know, has some some a lot of background to it? >> Yes. You know, it just showed me growing up how much hard work it takes to be great at whatever you want to do. Um my dad's very hard worker, my uncle's hard worker, my cousin Bron Breaker is very hard worker. So, it kind of just showed us how hard we need to work to be great at what we want to do. Yep. How many of these guys, has anybody like challenged you to wrestle? Um uh Do you get that a lot? >> Uh in college I got in a few wrestling matches during practice that my coaches weren't too happy about, but it hasn't happened yet here. Uh were you putting on them like WWE moves or were you putting on them >> Uh A famous quote Rich Rod said one after in a meeting was what kind of WWE bull crap was that? So. Now, as you're working on this football thing and trying to carve your career into it, you know, how long do you want to do this thing? Um as long as I can. I want to play football as long as I can. You know, I've been playing since I was, you know, 5 years old, you know, so I'll just play as long as I can.

title: TJ Hall on getting acclimated, special teams | Saints Rookie Minicamp
text: Couple days rookie mini camp, how things going for you? It's going good, man. I've been having fun. Uh it's been exciting, especially like meeting new guys here, all the rookies, free agents. Uh just getting out there to compete, man, it's been a blessing. Now, a lot of people wouldn't call this necessarily fun, the acclimation process where you're trying to get the information, trying to figure out things, but how's that part of it going? Yeah, uh I would consider it fun cuz uh the process is almost uh more fun than like the actual, you know, the game itself, you know, building up, you know, learning the playbook, practicing, working your technique. So, like to me that is fun and it's all part of football. You know, when you're out here and you, I guess, you know, going to different positions, how does that feel because that's one of the things that helps a a rookie, anybody, the versatility. Yeah, it definitely helps, especially like if you know all positions on the uh especially in the secondary, then it just bring more value and then it also helps the team out where if somebody goes down, you can step up and fill in. You know, also, I guess, special teams is one of those factors that goes into that also. Yes, sir. Yeah, definitely, you know, special teams plays a huge factor. Uh that sometimes comes down to a special teams play that to win a game, so you know, that's a huge factor. You know, when a team drafts you and they've got some guys in the secondary, but not necessarily seasoned guys, there seem to be some openings, how much optimism is there? Uh I feel like there's always optimism, you know, it's just uh it's a chance to go out there and compete, you know, no matter who's there, you know, I'm going to come each and every single day and give it my best, give it my all and that's only going to push not only myself, but the vets to push them to be better as well. You know, how much does this help you going forward because you guys come back now and you're a step up in in terms of getting closer to where the veterans are in the playbook? Yeah, yeah, it's definitely uh this whole process has been very helpful, you know, coaches have been harping on us to get in our playbook, you know, especially in the hotel room, you know, study, uh do what you got to do, so when you come out here and be ready.

title: Kellen Moore recaps Day 2 | Saints Rookie Minicamp
text: Second day of rookie camp. Good work. Another very similar day as you guys saw. Um had a few guys not out there, but that's just, you know, building maintenance plans for these guys and building these guys programs to get them ready to go for a football perspective. So again, there's a few guys that not out there, but that's just part of this process of getting to know these guys, getting uh them into our system and building these guys plans just so hey, they are ready to go. Uh particularly, you know, for training camp and all that sort of stuff, but just start building these guys up the right way for OTAAS and all that fun stuff. [snorts] >> Did Tyson get injured yesterday? No, no. Again, just similar for these guys. We finally get our hands on these guys. They've been through a lot, whether injuries last year, offseason, uh, training, and all that sort of stuff. We just put these guys in our system and similar to last year, you probably saw rookies who were, you know, in and out of different activities. And so, um, very similar to a number of these guys that didn't participate. >> Yeah, this would just be planned just based off of, uh, putting together a plan for him. Just to just clarify so I guess people understand. Why do why do some of these guys already need a maintenance plan on day two? Is that from things coming in or from you saw on the tracker or whatever >> things? It can be a combination of both things coming in. Obviously, uh Jordan had a number of things that came up last year during the season. So, hey, we got them in in our system now and let's just start building this thing the right way. And um you know, sim similar to a number of guys we had last year as well. Well, would that be a similar approach for him during the spring like during OTAA and stuff? >> Yeah. Yeah. I mean, early on this acclamation phase and so we'll get them in there and uh we'll just start building it the right way and u we'll take it kind of day by day. >> So, he was in the building. >> Yeah. Yeah. >> What did you like about Alan Har? He goes from D2 program in the senior. >> Yeah. Yeah. Uh really fun exposure. I think his story and his experience is always a fun part of this draft process. uh senior bowl, 30 visit, all that sort of stuff. You get a lot of exposure to different guys. And so, um, credit to him for just kind of, you know, that's one of those positive things of what a portal, an NIL world in college football actually creates a positive, you know, environment. So, it allows guys to compete and when they have opportunities to kind of take the next step, they can do it. And so, I think it allows these guys to be more prepared when they come to this level, uh, to be ready to go. And so, uh, you know, fired up to have him. >> When you mentioned yesterday that Barry Brown is also receiver. Is that what you heard? [laughter] >> Yeah, I think uh certainly uh you know he he's had a lot of success at receiver and so we certainly see that vision for him in addition to the the return game that obviously everyone notices. >> Uh kickers just kicked yesterday so they weren't uh they weren't kicking today. So just a one day. Tell >> when you have your lineman out there and they can't get a whole lot of work done physically. I guess how much does it help to have had Jeremiah at the bowl and have had a good look at it? >> Yeah, interior D lineman um offensive lineman obviously this is going to be a little bit of a challenging um venue for them to participate and so it's a ton of individual work. It's a ton of uh teaching and uh the physical component will come. Obviously, hey, a couple of these guys we did see at the Senior Bowl. Again, added bonus to this whole entire draft process. for the second year guys who who are out here. How does is that their decision to come out or is that a request from coaches? Like how does that kind >> It's b b b b b b b b b b b b b b b b b b b b b b b b b b b b b b b b b b b b b b b b based off of what their activity was last year, if they just remained on practice squad, they become available for us. And so um you know, it's a great opportunity for those guys. And what's fun is to see those guys. A number of them were in our camp in our rookie camp last year and now see them. They're the they're the savvy vets out there knowing everything what to do and they they played well. >> So if they were on the practice squad that didn't necessarily >> Yeah. If they didn't get Yeah. If they didn't get an acred season. So then they become available. So we just had a couple of them. I think what do we have? Probably >> six, I think. Yeah. >> And if they are eligible, is that their option that they can use or does >> Yeah, we certainly talk to Yeah, we'd love to have them and you know, obviously these guys are all on board with that. >> Do you like to to throw a lot of guys like in this like people kind of line up a lot of places, a lot of motion like do you kind of like to see how they respond to decent amount of info? I think taking the guys who obviously we have visions for from a draft pick perspective, free agency perspective, they're going to be with this whole journey. Essentially, they're a week behind our veterans. And so our whole goal is really to expose them to what they just missed out on with the veterans so that now Monday when they show up, they just hop in there and they're, you know, wait room's going to be different. They got to work through an acclamation phase with Ted, but other than that, they're with the veterans and they're at the same pace and speed that those guys are at. And so, yeah, there's a few things that may be a little bit challenging. a few uh pieces. It's not a cookie cutter, you know, stale, very simple uh exposure, but I think that's a positive for particular those guys who obviously will be here for uh the long haul. And so, uh we just want to get them up to speed as quickly as possible. >> And like as you're looking at child guys, like how can they make an impression? Like what what does someone need to do in this little like two day period, [clears throat] 30 snaps? Like how can they >> Yeah, first impressions are huge. Um do you know what you're doing? Uh, obviously there's a production standpoint to highlight yourself, but I think one of the biggest things is you got to showcase that you know what you're doing and know what the responsibilities are. Uh, if you can't get past that step, it's going to be challenging to show the anything else. >> Back to the line and I saw you checking him out a little early offensive line. Um, anything with Jeremiah that like kind of impressed you so far as >> Yeah, just a just a strong strong guy. Uh, obviously we saw what he progressed through u, you know, coming from Auburn, you know, his exposure there playing both sides of the football and all that sort of stuff. Um, yeah, these are challenging exposure. So, again, most of it's going to be individual work with uh with the offensive line coaches working through the individual techniques and then some of the communication stuff which is huge. And so, u you know, good first impression. >> What did you like when the kickers? >> Yeah, they they just kicked outside u and so we put them outside and um again, both of them were able to kick which was great. Went through that whole process just like you would in season with our kickers. Go through a full kicking routine of getting those guys as much exposure there. And so, um, positive experience. >> It's assuming that you've, uh, made some changes in how you're operating and like schedule you put together after having the first year as a head coach last year. Is there anything you'd be able to share just about what you're doing differently this year or any lessons you have from last year? >> I think it's just clean up, clean up things. Uh, try and be as efficient as possible as we as we go through this. I think our guys are have really attacked this offseason program so far. Uh, I mean, we got just about everyone here. um you know and these guys are going for it every day and they're with Ted and those guys in the weight room and now that we're getting into some of the football part uh the way these guys are attacking this thing um it's really awesome really awesome the leadership that's kind of coming coming through as we kind of build this thing uh this way and so u they're really competitive we're doing a lot of competitive things uh just from a team standpoint team building standpoint and so I think it's been great to see all that energy >> to follow up on the thing you're talking about with the rookies being on the same page as the veterans for next year trying to get them on the stage Is that common across the NFL or is that like something that you wanted to bring this year? Like does that take place everywhere? >> I would say it's heading more towards that direction. Um, I think there's not every team's necessarily doing a rookie camp this year just because I think so much of it again is the education of these guys have been through a lot the last few months and a lot of it isn't necessarily football u work, you know, it's it's training for obviously their testing, the travel that comes with the draft process and then these guys kind of feel like urgency that okay, I got to get going because you know all these veterans are three plus weeks ahead of us and so it's about an acclamation process building these guys up again. And um we want these guys to get acclimated as quickly as possible with the vets. So our approach is hey give them as much information as we can just so they're not too far behind and then uh we'll catch them up as we go. >> And had that changed from like your time in Dallas or Los Angeles or anything? >> Probably the last few years it's kind of shifted more towards this uh I think being with Brandon LA we kind of did a similar approach same in Philly and so the last couple years it's been uh more of this approach. I think it's good. We get enough exposure. We still see these guys again you guys saw it. We did some seven on seven. There's some competitive components, so you get to see these guys move around, but again, we're not um going to comp compromise their progress through this whole offseason program. >> Tyson, would it be fair to say that it's like still that the hamstring kind of ramping up from? >> Yeah. Yeah, he dealt with the hamstring and obviously, you know, again, we just want to build these guys up the right way. And so, um, that's what's awesome about these last couple days is our training staff, our sports performance guys. They really get involved with this, get get around these guys. They get some field work. Um, and then we kind of put these guys on different plans just to be really successful. >> And then by like training camp, the expectation would be 100% like we'll probably see some of this throughout. >> Yeah. Again, every guy's going to be on different plans here. Again, we focus on, hey, building these guys up the right way through this whole offseason program. When you get to the veterans will be here, you know, again, we you guys will see phase three. They'll be veterans in similar plans where, hey, they may be limited to certain exposures. Again, we're building these guys up so that the whole goal is OTAAS is just a continuous build up and then they when they leave this place, they just keep going on their own for a few weeks and then training camp, we just keep going. And so, uh, different than, you know, OTAAS and take this long break and go back to ground zero, ground, you know, first level, like let's just keep building. And so, that's the goal for all these guys. I know we were talking about uh you had mentioned Delp's uh ability with special teams, you know, yesterday and his potential with that, but you know, from the first two days, I I know there was a lot of talks heading into the draft about his traits and his impressive traits he shows and how it could resonate at NFL level. Have you kind of gotten confidence in in that like through any traits that he's shown through these first couple of days and and uh what [snorts] else has impressed you about? >> Yeah, I'd just say good first exposure. U obviously he has athleticism. We saw that on film. um the physicality I think in which he plays with will show up as we progress particularly in pads that'll be a big part of this thing because um you know from a tight end perspective you know that's a deep group now which is a positive not everyone's going to catch a football every time and so uh guys are going to do some dirty work and he's certainly shown he's capable of that and then the special teams component I think is going to be an added bonus you know some of these guys you know maybe uh Delpin for example they don't do as much special teams in college u you know because they're premier players they're playing on offense and defense and they're playing these, you know, very defined roles. Well, here we're going to ask them to do that and that's going to be a huge part of, uh, our success and we need these guys to really embrace it. And so, uh, it's been great to see those guys out there. I mean, special teams from college to the NFL, it's very different. I mean, the kickoff's different, the punt setup's different. These are all a lot of times trained skills that these guys don't have as much exposure to. >> I saw Jeremiah and Will Clap having a moment earlier with Will getting into that new role. How do you maybe see that bridge, if you will, between like him switching over to between him and like the older coaches? >> Will's awesome. I've been fortunate. I was with him in LA. Then last year, obviously having him here, I think what was a great opportunity, a blessing in disguise. Um, obviously he got hurt and that's a challenge, but we got kind of got to see him in a different lens. And the way he kind of started mentoring guys last year and putting himself in a little bit more of a coaching uh approach to the week, I thought was really beneficial. And so when we uh Jar had the opportunity to go to Pittsburgh, um you know, we're excited for Jarry, but we obviously had to make a decision and it was a really simple decision at that point. I mean, Will's Will knows this thing inside and out. He's just played he's played at a really high level for a number of years in this league and so his communication with these guys, I think, is going to be excellent. >> When it comes to the star slot position, you mentioned before that there were players in the building that you feel like could potentially compete there. Are are any of those players in scenarios like this Do you feel like you could find somebody that also from this group competes there too? >> Yeah. Yeah. We got veterans, we got young guys. Uh we got a lot of guys that we're excited to give them exposure and so um that'll be great. >> With a guy that's returning like Jaden Price, is is he somebody that could be in that consideration? What have you seen from him that maybe could get >> Yeah, JP's done a nice job. Um you know, he hopped in, he played UFFL right into our our season and just started playing football. He's kind of gone through this year- round process so far. And so, uh again, I think it's a great example. He's a veteran and when veterans come to these type of opportunities, you like to see that they're kind of the guys running the show and and that's what you see.
