So, you you know, you have a more of the guys that that uh break tackles and are are you know, vertical guys or you know, it depends on what scheme we're running, you know, what returner we have. If it's a smaller faster guy, then you have to run different schemes with those kind of guys. So, it all it all depends on who who shakes out and who's it who's it going to be, you know, like I said, there's in in each of those positions in the in the punt returner spot and the kick returner spot, there's five or six, seven guys in each each of those spots that are going to battle that out and we'll see how it shakes out. It became clear last year that Gifford and Neal really kind of took over a leadership role on the coverage units. Were there were there younger guys that began to emerge throughout the season that you're sort of excited to see sort of move into those, you know, leadership positions? Well, I think that, you know, anytime you have guys like like Gifford and Neal that can come in and set the tone for your whole group, it's been awesome. But all those young guys that got to play, especially late, you know, I thought they did a really good job. Um, you know, Siegel did a heck of a job for us. Martin started coming along there towards the end. You know, and I think that, you know, we got a new group of of young kids coming in that that we're excited about. So, that [clears throat] are long and they're fast and everything like that. So, it's going to be interesting to see how that all shakes out as well. The good thing is, like I said, it's >> the core group of of the our entire group last year in the first year of a system, I thought they did a hell of a job buying into our standard, creating a standard here. Did we finish the way we wanted to finish? Absolutely not. Um, but I thought they did an overall a really good job and we're really excited about the the new guys that that we added and and uh and we we got to be more physical. We got to get, you know, >> I think we got to tackle better. Um, but certainly the the the depth of what we have now and the year of experience will help us, I think. I want to ask about Dugger, whether he kind of caught your eye as as someone who could potentially, you know, be >> Sure, if you're that big and that long and that fast, you certainly should be able to help us, that's for sure. And he's a great kid from what I understand and and very sharp, too. So, that'll that'll really help us. One of the best better special teamers last year in the college football playoffs was Kamara. Blocked the punt against Miami in the national championship game. Have you seen him as a special teamer? What do you What do you think? >> all those those like D end kind of transfers over or they going to be a linebacker? Are they going to be a D end? Certainly specifically with these new kickoff rules that we have, right? It's turned into more of a two-hand kind of deal and those bigger guys are really valuable now and it it never used to be that way. Kamara, there's there's a bunch of guys in the mix with with that too as well. The the Robert Beal kind of bodies, right? The bigger taller guys, the D ends that that really help guys on teams and and we're looking forward to having all those guys for sure. Okay. Couple more guys. There's a bunch of guys in the league. What have you seen from that group in particular? I'm sorry, I didn't hear you. >> Okay. The Australian Oh. >> Yeah, that's um I think that that all those Australian guys obviously they're they are super talented guy. They've got um I mean seems like they've had a ball in their hands since they were tiny kids the way they can make that ball move and all the different kicks that they have and stuff like that. I really think that the NFL has done a great job of bringing all those guys in and and uh certainly you know, you see it all through college now that a lot of Australian punters and kickers and stuff like that and and uh they they have some kicks that that that are hard to replicate and they're hard to catch for returners and so it'll be interesting to see how this this plays out with the punter position for sure. You guys were towards the top statistically in in all of the league. How do you plan to duplicate that this year um going into this season? Well, like I said, I think there's a lot of things that that we did well. Um you know, I think we still got to continue to play smart. We we didn't commit a lot of penalties this year or last year. I think we got to continue that. We got to um certainly want to shore up a lot of things that that I didn't like uh in the off season here um and and I think that there's a lot overall of of like I I wouldn't say that um that I'm unhappy with last year at all. I thought that like I said the standard that we set and the overall buying of the entire team was awesome and you got to hand it to the players. They they did a hell of a job and they they bust their ass for us and did a great job. Um like I said our finish was not nearly good enough for the standard that we need here and and that's going to be a big part of what what we're we're getting after them this this off season and uh we've got to finish better. We got to be more physical. We got to tackle better and uh you know, while we had a good season decent season last year, it's not nearly good enough for us to win a championship and we need to help our team more period. Last one, Eric. What went into the decision not to bring back Morsehead? Well, I think that number one that you know, obviously I have a relationship with Thomas. There is not a human being that I respect more than Thomas Morsehead as a player and as a as a uh you know, as a as a friend and as a man. I think that part of that that's part of the business, right? And we're excited as hell about the two guys that we have. but it's always [clears throat] you're always trying to to uh you know, get guys in to compete and everything like that and there's a lot of stuff that goes that goes into that as well. The contractual sides and stuff like that. So um I think Teemu's still got a bunch in him. I I really do. I think he'll play uh some more and um but we're really super excited about the two guys we have and we'll see how it shakes out. Thanks, guys.

title: Coordinators Preview Rookie Minicamp, Share Early Expectations for 49ers Newcomers | 49ers
text: What's going on, guys? >> I'm doing absolutely outstanding. Fired up to be here and talk to you guys. What's going on? >> Well, you were you were hired, I believe, uh, early February, our first chance to to meet you. So, very nice seeing you up there. What have you been doing as far as when you take over uh as defensive coordinator? What are the first things on your plate when you come to a new building? >> Um, it's pretty simple. You know, you get a chance to go evaluate, you know, all the guys that are in this building, our current players, the people that we have. You get a chance to, you know, really marvel with some of the talent that they've been able to acquire over here over the last couple of years. you know, being this division not too long ago, you got a chance to know a lot of the guys and know a lot about all the guys and then obviously the people that they acquire, you know, through the draft, but you really want a good feel on, you know, the people that are here, what they have, what's already in place, what they've done really well. Um, and I was really close to this building, uh, from afar. So, that happened pretty easily and pretty seamlessly with some of the coaches that we do have. >> You kind of alluded to it just then over the years, Kyle has said he's wanted to bring you here many times. How close were you over the years to being here and and what made right now the right time? >> Uh I don't I I don't know. You got to ask Cal how close. Um because you're you're either on the the the stick where you know we went to Super Bowl together in 2016. Um and easily could have come come then um if allowed to um deny there from that standpoint. Nothing in a negative way but um you know it's always you know nice to be wanted within your own building as well. So being able to stay there over the course of the years and then um obviously when things didn't work out the first time and we were let go in Atlanta um Kyle's always a person that I talked to regardless of the situation um but I had an opportunity to go be a coordinator and you know and obviously you guys had great people in place at that point and you know Deno was in place and going to be the coordinator but um as you know all coaches want to be around guys that they want to be around so when you get an opportunity to add people to it like you guys did with Gus Brighter last year was probably going to something similar opportunity at that point. But got fortunate enough was able to go with Shawn who's another guy that you always talk to when these kind of things come up and uh went to LA and had some success there and was able to go along and um become a head coach again back in Atlanta. So this time when it came open um had a couple different opportunities. um you're never expecting it, but you really, you know, not expecting those things to happen. And you just kind of you sit back, you you kind of take some time with family and do some of the things that we all want to do, and we're not looking at you guys. Um and get the opportunity to go out there and make some real decisions. And um Kyle was, you know, someone that you you love working with, love working for. Not to say that you wouldn't like working with other people as well, but Kyle's definitely one of those people you always want to work with from our time being in whether it was Tampa. Um the original time worked together when we're both young puppies or the second time we worked together where in DC um and being able to be around his father and be around a Shanahan family and the tradition and the the culture that they're able to form and and really molded me throughout my career since I was around a Shanahan to be honest. In terms of um defensive philosophy, we're seeing across the league more fiveman fronts um pretty pretty generally. What what is your or I guess the question is why do you think that is and what's your philosophy on fiveman fronts? >> You know, these guys are getting, you know, they're harder to defend, you know, just the the coordinators in this league, you know, like let's not kid ourselves. People want to see offense. Um the rules have changed in different ways for you to do different things. So, you got to have some multiplicity in your front, you got to have multiplicity in the back end. Um, you got to be able to do different things. Um, you like to be able to do those things when you decide to do those things and use them as um terms where you can, you know, dictate, so to speak, but, you know, we have been a four down rush team and we've done a nice job in it. I know we've uh dibbled and dabbled a little bit last year, even with Robert Salah, which I have so much respect for and what he was able to do and how we did it. But, you know, I was able to accumulate and acquire a bunch of different ideas and thoughts. u along my stops uh with the different people that I work with whether it's been Jim Hlin in Washington you know where they were strictly a three four base pitch team or really being able to do some of the different things that we did last year being able to mix it up uh being able to play some four down stuff um being able to play a bunch of five down stuff so like I think you got to be able to move around and and kind of move those chest pieces to be able to help you go out there and really uh do your best to stop these really explosive offenses that's okay >> sorry Kyle has talked a lot about when it comes to the development of a coach. He he credits his early time in Tampa getting to actually work on the defensive side of the ball to help him as an offensive coach and he's talked about uh different coaches having that experience. You obviously have worked on on both sides. How how much do you credit your work on the offensive side including with Kyle in Atlanta for your development as a defensive coach? >> I mean it's been um our whole career has kind of been uh the business of being nosy so to speak. So, like when Kyle came to um Tampa, fresh out of UCLA, you know, all fired up and eager, we were stealing his dad's zone scheme keeper game as much as he was stealing uh Tampa 2 and all different values that he wanted to bring to us. So, when we did all the cross training, even when we were young, it was constantly, you know, staff development within the building um with some of the better coaches that we have been around in our lifetime really. you know, Mike Tomlin was secondary coach and Monty Keifin was the defensive coordinator along with Ryan Marinelli and what he was able to bring with the original um a part of his attack front doing some of the different things sort of the stud that we had, you know, um very similar to that stuff and he was around a lot of good coaches and Joe Barry, all those guys. But we shared a bunch of information and then I got a chance to obviously work on defense in such a long time and when I was able to switch over to offense, you know, with Kyle in Atlanta um kind of having a the outside inversion of what the offense looks like, what it means and what it's going to do um to really get into the deep weeds of it and watch him game plan and watch him go through the process of a week of preparing for a different team. And then even when he left, being able to stay on that side of the ball and really develop and grow and, you know, as a person that can really go out there and formulate plays to go find open spaces and do different things that you want to do from an offensive standpoint, uh, was so much fun and so much um, different perspective than you had just going out there coaching defense, right? You can actually, you know, speak in their language, understand what some of the quarterback reads are, being able to be detailed enough to go out there and try to stop those things. uh being able to explain it to your players in a completely different way which was my strength when I went from defense to offense then being able to come back it still remains your strength so like you grow from all the experiences you uh you gain all experience with the people um and and I've really enjoyed the process of being able to switch back and forth now not many coaches in the national football league say they can coach on both sides of the ball and definitely not many can say they've been on a number one defense and a number one offense and coach sides of the balls in respective season so like I am u truly blessed uh truly feel it is like a definite benefit to being able to work in with Cal and being able to work around that type those type of people. Do >> you expect your defense to resemble what it looked like in Atlanta or is it going to be more of a continuation of what's been happening here the last few years? >> We definitely want to do what's best for our players. You know, you always going to do what they do really well. You know, Fred Warner is Fred Warner for a reason. Um I'm going to try to utilize those guys to the best of their ability to do some of their different things and be to have some additions to be able to go out there and ultimately to go try to win a championship. um whatever's required, whatever is needed to go do those things, those are the expectations and those are the things that we want to get done. So, um to say it's going to be more resemblant to me or more resemblant to them is going to be what's best for us in order to go win football games. And I think that's the best way to look at it, you know, u ultimately, you know, whatever it takes to go win football games, whatever it takes to go out there and get it done for us. >> What about the 49ers made you pick them? I know you said you had some other other teams, but what was it about this organization that felt right? didn't know all about the organization before, knew more about Kyle and knew more about Lynch. You know, obviously, um those are guys that I've been really close to just throughout the whole process of everything, right? having an ability to coach Lynch when I was a very young football coach. Uh being around that culture and what it meant and then having a chance to be a coach with Cal and being a coach with Cal in multiple spots and then having an opportunity to come out here and then you get out here and you see what everything is like, you know, what they've done together, you know, how they built this thing to be able to run the draft, be able to run the process, be able to run the standard of play. Uh being around these guys and then, you know, really competing against these guys, you get this healthy respect of just, you know, you love to be a part of that. you know, when you get a chance to go be a part of teams um like that, which I've been fortunate enough to do in the past, um it certainly made it like an easy choice for me, you know, like uh with all due respect to the people that I talked to because everybody that I talked to that actually called me got so much respect for those people. But, you know, Kyle um was was a great opportunity to come work here at the 49ers. And by being in Atlanta the last couple years, you got to see Mike Evans up close obviously and he's been in the league as long as he So, what is he going to do to Kyle's offense that you know so well and having faced it with McCaffrey at full strength and Brock back there? >> Yeah, I just think it's more about, you know, the people, you know, and like um what they can do for each other, I think it' be the most beneficial thing that those guys sit down and talk about and how they can make each other better. You know, Mike is a pain in the neck defending against him because he has so many skill sets and different things that he can do. And I'm sure Cal's going to find things that he didn't do as great and try to make it better. And when you do those things with great players, you you capture their attention right away. And when you capture your attention, you get the best from those guys. And I' I've seen it happen with a bunch of different guys in this past and I don't want to name their names because some of them been here, some of them have been other places, but when you get the best version of the players in the building, which I know Kyle can do, and along with the staff, you know, being around these guys to meet these guys, I'm really fired up, you know, being around Kubak, being around Mike, uh, being around all the different people that are here. I'm really fired to see what they can do with Mike and really fired up to see where he can grow um, here as a player. John Lynch said that you were you brought a lot of energy in the draft meetings and he said that when you really liked a player, you're like, "Hey, if we get that guy, we're we're gonna throw a pool party." >> Do we any pool party uh draft picks in this draft from your perspective? >> Honestly, it it it was a cool process for me to be a part of to find consensus with the organization. you know, I forget who just asked the question about, you know, defensive thoughts and ideas, but like it's it's cool to be able to try to express those things to those guys and those guys to formulate and find ways to be able to help you formulate those things, get those people in the building. Um, but there was certainly some pool party people, you know, both offense and defensively, you know, being nosy, having the ability to coach on offense and defense. You got a chance to see Stri got a chance to see all these different guys that you able to acquire on defense. and like the way and the manner that we went about getting them I thought was very unique and I thought was pretty cool to watch you know to watch all these guys and have such a respect for whether you're talking about RJ uh whether you're talking about Reek and some of the different guys that all a part of that process and along with the coaches and everybody in that room without scouts and everybody coming to these um real strong you know convictions I I think was uh was pretty cool. I thought it was a great process. I love being around it and it was definitely some pool party guys and uh that was that was a cool that was a cool thing >> like about you see from Romelo height >> come back to you got >> what did you see from Romelo height and Grayson Hall your two defensive line guys >> uh you know obviously um just going off what you guys know from here um you always want to have those pass rushers right and Romelo brings a certain ability to pass rush that he showed opposite of um his young teammate out there at Texas Tech and Romelo is going to come in here and be able to provide some of those things for us and be able to get into that room and really learn from one of the best Dline coaches in the world and and Chris Caceric and like and and Greg Scrugs and you know obviously Cam Brown and being able to get with those guys and be able to be the best version of himself. So like watching Romelo as a pass rusher, watching Romelo be able to go out there and do some different things, whether it be um in the pass game or whether it be even in the run game, you see all the things that we love, you know, about the guy, the wit, the stuff that he does, how he plays the game and all that stuff. He plays with high energy, you know, probably one of the highest energy guys in the draft that we saw and that that I was at least able to evaluate. So, extremely confident and fired about that. And no different with Halton, right? He gives that same type of interior presence. You know, last year you guys went out and had a big CJ and you had a big AC, you know, big time run stoppers, big time guys that can just get off the ball, disrupt, and do a bunch of different things. And you go out there and keep adding guys in those positions so you can get that constant role. And to be able to get those guys to roll through that cause obsolete disruption for everybody that we play against is something that you love. >> I'm curious, uh, when you and Kyle were in the Super Bowl versus the Patriots, you guys obviously came so close and this organization has done pretty much the same. Have you guys kind of had the chance to connect about that? And how how eager are you guys? >> How eager are you guys to bring the Bay Area and the Niners a Super Bowl? Yeah, like ultimately as a competitor is what you want to do. It's what you think about every single day. And then nothing would be more satisfying for me personally than to be able to come here and help this organization, um this head coach, this general manager, um this owner, um this team, the players that they have. You talking about Fred Warner and Nick Bossa and guys that absolutely you want to go win that thing for. You get kind of chills just just really thinking about it. like to have the ability to be to go do that and help people do that. That's what you coach for. That's the ultimate goal. >> Your going back with with Kyle and it's been a friendship for a long time. What do you think clicks between you two guys? >> Uh you know really u the ultimate thing with coaches that really are committed to each other is obsession. And um he has an obsession about football that's just, you know, unmatched. Um, and when you have that obsessive personality to be the very best at what you do, I think that's something that ultimately clicks when you're talking about coaches. Like there's going to be coaches in everybody's office. It's going to be cross trainining. Um, and it's already started to happen, you know, with, you know, Mick Lombardi on the offensive staff, myself, my own personal staff, being able to get with Matt Eva, being able to get with Jerry Gray, you know, some of the guys that were here like Chris Caceric, being able to go to their side of the ball with some of the young guys that are just eager to be the very best to be able to learn and keep growing. like that. It's just an obsession of football that makes you click. >> Have a good one, guys. How's it going? Good to see everyone. >> of excitement, too. Sorry. >> Yep. Um, I've been here the whole time. Um, but yeah, it's it's been good to have the players back for sure. Um, always a new energy when those guys are back in the building, getting to see them every day, reminding us why we like them so much and just just getting to be around the guys brings us energy every day. And, um, you know, I'm excited for this phase two, which starts next weeks, and then getting into our OTAAS. It'll be good. >> Your goals or what what do you try to accomplish when you get the rookies in here for the first time? >> Um, it's it's a combination of things. I think one, you really want them to start digging into the installs, right? In the playbook a little bit and they get in the meeting room with the coaches. So, there's that part of it, the mental uh getting them on the field and just kind of get them getting them adapted to the drills they're going to be doing. Uh the way we practice, the way we work on the field, it's kind of just kind of I see it as kind of a two-day orientation for, hey, you're here for a couple days, you're in the classroom, you're on the practice field, you know how we want to work, you know the standard. All right? And then they and then they're here on Monday. they're out there on the field with the players and they're kind of they join the group. So, it's it's kind of that dual purpose and you want to see see what they can do. You got all these tryyout guys coming in, some of these free agents we signed, you kind of want to see how they look and and um you know, so just just all those things kind of we're evaluating it all. So, >> will any of your quarterbacks be on the field? >> Track? >> Uh I I believe Curtis is going to be out there. I'm not 100% sure, but I know Curtis uh is eligible to be in our mini camp. So, yeah, he might be out there throwing. >> That you guys signed Mike Evans and how do you plan on using him? >> How did I find out? Same way you guys did. Showed up on ESPN uh on that first day of of um free agency. We were ecstatic and fired up. Obviously, we had a plan. We we evaluated him and and had intentions to want to sign him and we talked about it and so but just to get it done was was incredible. How do we want to use him? I mean, he's a he's a Hall of Fame wide receiver. You know, he's a one-on-one matchup that that you can take advantage of when he's on the field and he's got one-on-one coverage. you want to get the ball to Mike, you feel like he's going to win. Uh he's about as competitive as they come. He's he's he's a guy who's going to win his matchups and it's just really cool to have that alpha type of player out on the field at that position for us again. And um you know, we're going to use him the way he's been used his whole career and hopefully get a few more things out of him too along the way as we get him in our program. So >> it's an evolving process, but what what is kind of your shortterm vision for dribbling and then maybe what the what the long-term view is where you'd like him to get? I mean, short term it's got to be you got you got to go day by day with with anybody any new player. You gota you gota teach them the offense. You know they got to learn everything from the ground up. You got to teach them how you how you see the position. You know the fundamentals of playing wide receiver and and he's got to grow from the ground up. I mean and I don't think any player starts above that. They got to start there. And so that's the first part. And and just getting him acclimated to to our our playbook, our standard, our work ethic, and then our fundamentals, you And then I think long term, you know, I think you guys have kind of heard us talk about our vision for him. You know, he's a he's a big, fast, powerful football player and and he can help your he can help our offense in so many ways with the ball in his hand as a route runner without the ball in his hand is a huge strength of his. The way he plays his mindset and so he's a he's a complete football player and those guys make your team better. Um so he's going to affect the game in a lot of ways. That's our that's our vision for him as far as you know the long term for sure. What did you see in Curtis Schwarz last year? What's the next step for him uh this off season? >> Got to see him. I think I think it was a couple weeks he was able to practice um and love the arm talent. You know, he's a he's a heck of a thrower. Um he's big. He's strong. He can stand in there and make every throw on the field. And we we saw that from him when he was able to be on the field. Um super bright guy, you know, absorbs our playbook, our our offense really well. He he hasn't missed a beat on that end. I'm excited to go see him out there and just put it all together and get reps um with with with our guys and and consistency and stack days and just see how he gets better. Uh we have high hopes for him. Um but I'm just excited about him as a player. >> I'll mention that uh Kaylin Black was the number two running back on your on your board this year. What uh made you so excited about Kaylin when you watched his tape? >> He's a guy who, you know, he really he kind of grew on us over time. the more we watched, studied these backs and really stacked them all together, you saw a guy who got the most out of every run that he put on tape. I mean, I mean, when he touched the ball, he was maximizing every play. Um, whether that be an explosive run where he was going through the line or it was a run where it wasn't blocked very well and he was going to get you four or five five yards, he's just he's a really physical, tough runner. He's got good speed. Um, you know, and and to me what I loved about watching him was when you saw their team Indiana get to the playoffs. He was one of the best players on the field. He was a big reason why they won the national championship. Uh, he had some huge games and some huge moments and just a competitive dude. And so we're we're real excited about him. >> When you guys walked off the field against Seattle and you watched that film, what stood out to you and and have you guys added some players this off season that maybe have improved you in those problem areas? Um, I mean there's a lot of things that didn't go well in that game, you know, as a team. I wouldn't just say offensively, but you know, when you look at our our games against them last year overall, you know, you gota they have they're talented across the board defensively, but you there's things you got to do to beat those guys. You got to run the ball better because they want to play their two shell defenses and and uh but you got to run the ball better. So, we we got to improve in that area, you know, and and whether we're adding players or we're improving our scheme starts with that. Um, you know, you got to win. You got to beat their corners. They have great corners that want to challenge you one-on-one. You got to get players who can win one-on-one matchups and who who you can make plays to on the outside. I think we we we tried to address that and and just and just add more depth and more talent at the receiver position. So, but you know, all that's all said and done, you got to go out there and play better football and better and execute better. And so, I'm not going to sit here and say we've solved all those problems. It's we got to get better as a team and and and compete better. So, yeah. Another strippling question that we've heard that he's you guys have him in his gold helmet guy and that means a lot. What have you already picked that up from him just when he's been here or over the process to get him here and what does that mean to you? >> Yeah. Um you you you definitely pick it up when you're interacting with them in the draft process when you're meeting with these guys and you're you're doing your interviews. Those guys stand out, you know, and just the way that they carry themselves, the way they communicate. Um, you know, Hank, our our receiver coach, it stood out to him right away. This guy's different. You know, this guy's a pro. This guy's all about the right things. And you get that feel for them when you get to know him in the draft process. Um, I haven't gotten to be around him a lot yet. I will this weekend and I will move him forward. And I'm sure those traits will come out, you know, and and that's couldn't ask for anything more than that. But it's just a starting point now. We got to go out there and play and grow as a player. So, um, but just getting to know the guy, you really those those characteristics stand out. the offense >> last season. How do you evaluate that aspect of the talent versus >> Yeah. That's what you look for first. To be a productive NFL player, man, there's there's got to be one or two traits that you have that's that so elite you can do differently than everybody else. Uh you want to find those things, but always within the framework of the team. >> Yeah, I think you have to have demonstrated communication skills. Um, it doesn't have to be um where you've done it your whole life, you know, like where, okay, that's all I've ever done, you know, like some kids grow up as a quarterback from eight years old. It doesn't have to be that, David. But what it does have to be, there has to be confidence. There's got to be belief. Um, it's got to be firm because that voice is used in a lot of ways. Sometimes to give the call, sometimes it's to also let somebody know this is not how things are going to go. So, um there's a number of candidates that we have, but that would be at the top of my list like demonstrated ability to think under pressure. >> Real time processing >> real time and uh that ability for those players that have that thinking under pressure and quite often we try to make here at practice as stressful as he can. You're at your best when they're already finishing the call. Like, you're starting to make a call, you know, through the headset and before you're done, you see the person turning and starting the conversation. So, it takes a while to get to that spot where you can be in concert. Um, but the more you do it, you know, the more connected you become with the play caller and that helps too. >> You create that atmosphere here and I mean it's a three-day camp with a lot of try out guys or or does that, you know, lack of cohesion make it even better? >> I I think it's too early to test right now. It's the first uh go around. Let's just see, you know, communication. Is there urgency that goes with it? But as we get into the full team being together beginning on Monday and then through spring ball, that's really when you can kind of test it. This one is more uh let's get the function down and get to those skills before we uh turn up the heat too high. How are you? >> Yeah, just in fact got some, you know, the chance to spend some time with him today after our walk through to go in and it's the football knowledge also that goes with it. Um Josh has been somebody at Tennessee that's been versatile. He can drop, he can rush. That's why he's here to rush. But I'm excited um to have that type of length get off demonstrated pass rush ability. Um, I found the more of that that you have and develop it. We were talking about traits earlier, how important that is. He has that and we look forward to developing that trait to see if we can take him from this space into the next one. >> He has not told me. >> I do. >> Yes. >> Yeah. and uh you know coming out of Jacksonville and some of the different spots what I see right off the bat is you know at corner good length and the ability to match you know some of the taller receivers down the field and so those are a few of the things that you want to get into the evaluation can a corner track the ball down the field and sometimes just catch the flash of the ball and so those are the things that you're looking for at that spot um in Donte's scheme there'll be times when they're up playing on the line of scrimmage and times that we're off. And so those are the things that will start the process of training him on. But um I'm excited to see where he can take it. >> Had in the building for a couple months. What are you learning about him stylistically? >> I think from a leadership standpoint, I'll start there first. Man, is he organized, like impeccably organized. He's got a very detailed thought and approach to how things go from the way he meets with the defensive staff to the way he meets, you know, with the players. So, I like that approach that there's just, you know, he hits every single step along the way. As a player, you like that because he's thorough. He goes through all the steps. It's not gray. There's a lot of clarity. Um, even though at times it can seem, you know, complex to what we're doing, there's actually a lot of clarity that goes with it. So that's the part from a leadership standpoint that I've seen so far like the extreme organization and clarity of the teaching. >> To that point, what have you seen different? >> I think it's fun to see him install the whole thing, you know, in front of the room and identity of what we'd like to be of the different teaching. So there's quite a bit of new terminology, you know, for the players that, you know, were here from 24 and 25. So to see the different things that we're emphasizing um and him right in the front of it all, it's been excellent. One of the things I've been impressed by him is his ability and the staff to really function together. Uh like our receiver group as a coaching staff, I don't think you could come into a better space than to learn from Bobby and Wes and Andre. Like the amount of experience the three of them have together in the National Football League, it's it's incredible. And so they're able to share different things, different points of view, vibe off one another. As a coach, that's the type of environment that I'm looking for to see their vibe together. So that might be just one small example of him listening and also allowing some of the guys to make their imprint on the offense as well. >> Got time for two more. Yeah, I think the first part um like yeah it's totally expected and it's awesome in a way like as coaches we're also excited um for them it's their first NFL practice and we're here and so the first thing man like there's no expectations just like let's go through a great practice and that's where I start I want to see them communicate I want to see them go the practice intensity is going to be low but what I want to see from them is just their intent I saw it in walk through, we'll see it here. So, it's just kind of like the first step in onboarding somebody into like a really successful year. And so, it's an important step, but let's not make it bigger than that. Also, um there's a whole another set when all the veterans come back. Um how do they fit and where does that go? This is the type of team you'd want to be a part of as a rookie because there's people that would be looking out for you that have your best interest. We have not. >> Y >> I I can remember remarking to him um after a game. It might have even been at at Carolina. I just spoke to the competitor, you know, of who he is and what he stands for. And so I can remember him as, you know, a first time player coming up and competing against him. I said, "Man, you you hang in there. Like you got a lot to offer." and like he for damn sure did. And so I think it's kind of one of the my favorite parts of the NFL because of like the competitive nature of people going for it and I think uh he really represented that. >> Got time for one more. >> There's conversations but nothing official until the schedule comes out because that's where it could change. So what we do often times at from combine to league meetings say hey if it works out where you know we have the practice together would you be interested? So there's definitely some teams that we would like to um if it lines up you know to where we're practicing whether it's here or elsewhere. I like what it can bring. I like the different looks. I like the competitive nature of that. So there's definitely some guys that you want but until it becomes official with the league then we right when that happens kind of like are we in? Yeah we're good or no we're not. So, but we plan on that. We'll just play it out as it comes. >> All right. >> All right. Thanks everybody. You guys have a good one.

title: Billy Schrauth on Bucs' Offensive Unit: ‘Fired Up’ | Press Conference | Tampa Bay Buccaneers
text: How y'all doing? What do you think your first impression of working with Kevin Carberry and Andrew Mitchell? Um, awesome. You know, I'm learning a lot. What are some of the biggest changes that you'll have to make or even some of the biggest differences that you've noticed coming up to this level? Um, you know, I've been in the north my whole uh whole career, so it's warm down here. I don't think that's a secret. Um but, you know, I think football's football. I love the game. All those guys in that locker room love it. Um, you know, just grateful to be a part of it. You look at this Bucks defensive line that you'll be going up against in training camp and even in the OTAs but when the pads come on, you've got kind of a a 350-lb monster like Vita Vea. You've got a very quick, agile guy like Calijah Kancey. Uh anything those two different body types, contrasting styles will help develop you as a player? Yeah, I think it's awesome. You know, you get get to work a little bit of everything. Um constantly, you know, fine-tuning technique and you know, having a having a plan to to succeed. There are some things that might be hard to kind of practice and get used to. With that in mind, what are kind of the most important things that you look to work on in times like this where you're not in pads being kind of honing your technique more? three things, you know, eyes, your hands and your feet. You can always kind of fine-tune those things and um you know, just keep getting better technically. Will you try to stay down here and and and get acclimated to everything in the off-season? >> Yeah, 100%. Yeah. And there's guys on this roster that have made that transition, you know, coming from from the north. It takes a little bit of time. Yeah. Get your body adjusted to the heat and the sports science guys have told us that before. 100%. >> Get more efficient at sweating and things like that. And it can be hard, especially for bigger guys, on top of the fact that you have to wear all those pads. Yeah. And those come on. Totally. When you um when you get drafted by this team, like what's what's the top thing that you're going to bring to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers? And then what's the one thing that you really want to work on once you get acclimated to this system and improve in your rookie year? Yeah, um I'm going to bring energy to the guys. Um they're going to feel me. Um you know, I always try to give dudes energy and and not take it. I think that's number one. and then yeah, I think there's always room to improve, you know, uh Xs and Os-wise, physically getting stronger. This position's built on strength and power and I think, you know, always improving that. When do you find that that like if you're one of those people that has that reservoir of energy, do you find that that's most helpful for your teammates in the dog days of summer, in practices, is it most beneficial in the fourth quarter of of close games, or when you just want to run the ball down your opponent's throat? Um I think it's I think it's in everything, you know, I think it's when you're in the locker room, I think it's certainly when you're on the field in the fourth quarter and things are getting tough. Somewhere along uh I ain't got to try to, you know, prove anything. I'm not, you know, I I can be myself and I take a lot of comfort in that. Good. All right. Thank you very much. title: Ted Hurst Preparing to Play X Receiver | Press Conference | Tampa Bay Buccaneers
text: Congratulations on graduating by the way. >> Thank you. >> So, first workout out there. They throwing a lot at you obviously in these uh these mini camps. How do you think it went? You know, he told me like, you know, I have to get in shape coming in. You know, he just running drills and running short routes and all of that. So like for you, is there one particular spot that you feel like you're kind of honing in on a little bit or you kind of learn it all right now? >> X position for sure. >> You had a chance to meet any guys in the room yet veterans at all or >> Oh yeah, not not not yet. Do you feel like you still got something to prove? Where's your mindset right now? >> Yeah, I definitely feel like, you know, I still got something to prove. There's a lot of doubters on, you know, my my potential and where I can go at, you know, in this profession, but you know, I I you know, I have that talk with myself and it's kind of like, you know, um a little fuel to my fire. I see. >> You mentioned you could have gone, you know, left Georgia State, you decided to stay there, but then when you went to the Senior Bowl and got to compete against, you know, guys another level and you dominated. How much confidence did that give you and and and the ability to show scouts what you were capable of? >> Yeah. Yeah. I say I got, you know, great confidence, but I believe, you know, if I prepare myself the right way every time, it doesn't matter who I go against. You you mentioned talking to yourself like um I don't know if you're comfortable revealing this, but like what are some of those conversations you have? Like are we talking about like daily affirmations and things like that? >> Yeah. Yeah, definitely. Uh I start my morning off. I actually uh got this book. It's called One Minute with God. And I start my day off by reading that book and you know that's confidence and you know God's a big part of my life. So I I I use that to you know I say start my day. How how has uh how has God uh impacted your your football journey, >> man? Yeah, I've been lucky to, you know, not run into any crazy injuries. You know, it also gave me a opportunity for, you know, other people to look at me and, you know, just coming from where I come from, a lot of guys don't get that opportunity and he's just been amazing financially, helping me out and everything. I believe that that comes from God. >> How do you like Tampa so far? >> It's hot. It's hot. Yeah, it's hot in Georgia. Yeah, it's a it's a little more hot out here though for sure. >> We get we do get a breeze though. Like I mean being not landlocked does allow some some breeze. What you really got to worry about is when those flags are not moving upstairs when they're stationary. >> Oh yeah, >> it gets bad like in August and July. >> Yeah. They said around training camp it's going to get even crazier. >> You got time to acclimate though. It's a process. >> Said even yesterday like that's a big thing at the start of rookie man camp seeing how guys adjust to the heat. You feel like you'll be able to handle that for? >> Yeah. Yeah, I'll be all right. Just give me about a week. About a week, I'll be okay. >> If I remember correctly, you caught the last the last uh pass of of practice, I think, yesterday. Like the importance for you because a lot of times, especially when you are physically fatigued, mental fatigue, like that's that's when you have to kind of look for for guys to maybe like, you know, do they have the same level of concentration? Then how important is it for you to finish practice on a high note? >> Yeah. Um, I kind of always tell myself, you know, my brother's really hard on me about what's my why. My older brother had a had a daughter and you know he kind of paved the way for me in my profession and where I'm at today and and I got a younger brother and I feel like you know if he can use my name to open the door for him then you know that's amazing. >> Can you tell us a little bit more about your older brother? >> Yeah man, my brother is a kind of um you know my backbone, my right-hand man at the same time. U he's amazing. Graduated college um in chemistry. I don't know. He's a he's a nerd. um played football for four years. Um >> where did he go? >> At Vadosa State, um got injured twice, shook back from both of those. So I commend him for that. You know, I know that can be, you know, pretty challenging, you know, mentally and physically, and uh he won a championship in high school, won a championship in college. So yeah, he went to play arena ball actually and won a championship there. So commends to him. Ted, as you enter the NFL, what is the the best attribute you bring to the Buccaneers? And what's the one thing you really want to work on at this level? >> Um, yeah, I'll just say I bring value. He said, you know, this the guys I have in my room. This where I feel you can play at. This where I feel you can do, you know, and if you have the opportunity to do that, you know, you're going to put yourself in position to be where I'm at today.
